Name: HP Image Assistant
Description: HP's BIOS, firmware and driver update engine, packaged as a real MSI with a weekly scheduled task so it keeps running after the deployment finishes.
Awkwardness: HP's own Intune guidance wraps hpia.exe in an Install.cmd and detects on "the file HPImageAssistant.exe exists". That rule can never go from true to false, so once a device has any version of HPIA it looks compliant forever and a newer HPIA is never deployed. The underlying problem is that a SoftPaq extracts rather than installs: nothing is registered, there is no entry in Programs and Features, no version for Intune to compare, and the documented uninstall is a recursive delete. Shipping the extracted files as an MSI instead gives Intune a ProductCode and a version to work with, and gives the device a genuine uninstall.
DownloadNotes: Download the HP Image Assistant SoftPaq (spNNNNNN.exe) and hand it to MsiMaker as-is. MsiMaker runs the SoftPaq's own extractor (-s -e -f) to unpack it before packaging - extract only, so nothing is installed on this machine. You no longer have to extract it by hand first.
SetupFileHint: The HP Image Assistant SoftPaq you downloaded (spNNNNNN.exe, around 30 MB). MsiMaker extracts it to a folder of ~136 files (HPImageAssistant.exe with its Lib and Redist subfolders) and packages that.
Notes: Set Version to the HPIA version you extracted before building. Intune upgrades on the ProductCode, which is derived from that version, so a stale version means a package that never supersedes the one already out there.
Verified in this repository: built, installed, upgraded and uninstalled under msiexec. 27 MB of payload compressed to a 10.9 MB package.

The task writes reports and downloads under %ProgramFiles%\HP\HPIA, which Task Scheduler expands at run time. Keep them somewhere ordinary users cannot write. HP documents C:\ProgramData\HP, but ProgramData grants every user container-inherit write and add-subdirectory, and CREATOR OWNER full control over anything they create - so a SoftPaq staging folder there is a directory a standard user can plant a DLL in, which HPIA then loads as SYSTEM on the next run. C:\Windows\Temp is no better; it grants Users write and add-subdirectory too. If you move these, change ReportFolder and SoftpaqDownloadFolder together, and check the target with icacls first.
The registry Version value duplicates the project Version deliberately, as a detection anchor for anything that cannot read the ProductCode. Keep the two in step.
RunOnBattery is false and the random delay is two hours: a fleet that all wakes at 03:00 and downloads SoftPaqs at once is its own kind of outage.
CloseProcesses lists HPImageAssistant.exe, so an upgrade can replace files that a running analysis is holding open instead of silently scheduling a reboot nobody sees.

Verified means the package: built, installed, upgraded in place with HPImageAssistant.exe running, and uninstalled cleanly, checked against Windows Installer itself. It does not mean an HPIA analyze run has been exercised - that needs HP hardware. If you are the first to run it on a real device, check that the Reports and Softpaqs folders are created where you expect.

Tasks.Name: HP Image Assistant Update
Tasks.Description: Analyses the device against HP's reference and installs missing or out-of-date BIOS, firmware, drivers and software.
